power.title: Power Analysis Check

table.text: Sample size calculations are based on binary expression of extravasation (no harm vs any (mild, moderate, severe) harm) [1]. Local and international data report approximately 30-42% of IVs with intermediate to high-risk infusates result in extravasation injuries in hospitalised infants under conditions similar to our 'standard care' scenario [5] [6] [7] [8]. We conservatively estimate 20% of standard care alone participants will develop any extravasation injury (either mild, moderate, severe). Based on international observational [9, 10] and our pilot RCT [11] data we expect 10% of IV biosensor will develop an extravasation injury. That is, we expect the IV biosensor to have a 50% relative risk reduction in extravasation, compared to standard observation alone. With α=0.05 and power=90%, we are required to record outcome data on 266 participants in each group to detect a between-group difference of this size or greater (total sample=532). Previous trials demonstrate it is feasible to recruit this number over two years across the three study sites.

text.text: Background: Up to 20% of hospitalised infants with a peripheral intravenous catheter (PIVC) have an infusate-related injury.
The PATCH trial is testing whether an IV biosensor (ivWatch®) added to standard observation reduces infiltration and extravasation injuries compared with standard observation alone.
Methods: PATCH is a multicentre, type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation randomised controlled trial at three Queensland hospitals.

Infants under 1 year (≥1000 g) with a PIVC expected to remain more than 24 hours for intermediate-or high-risk infusates, antimicrobials or continuous fluids are randomised 1:1, stratified by site (four strata).
The target sample is 532.
Analysis: The primary outcome is any infiltration/extravasation injury (mild to severe harm, CCHMC Extravasation Harm Scale), confirmed by a blinded outcome assessment committee.
The primary analysis follows intention to treat and uses logistic regression adjusted for randomisation stratum.
The risk difference is estimated by standardisation, with the odds ratio also reported.
Secondary outcomes include injury severity, time to PIVC failure, dwell time, replacement PIVC, quality of life, skin injuries and serious adverse events.
This plan was finalised on 10/11/2026, during recruitment and before database lock or any unblinded analysis.

This multi-site, superiority Type-1 hybrid randomised controlled trial (RCT) will test the effectiveness and explore the value and implementation contexts of an intravenous (IV) biosensor (ivWatch®, ivWatch LLC, Newport News, Virginia, USA), compared to standard care, to detect extravasations and prevent extravasation injury.

The purpose of this document is to minimise bias and ensure transparency and internal validity for the findings of the trial by defining and making publicly available the analysis approach prior to reviewing or analysing any trial data.
This statistical analysis plan (SAP) will inform the analysis and reporting of the effectiveness findings of the trial.
It provides a detailed description of the primary and secondary trial effectiveness outcomes and the methods for statistical comparison.
-ANZCTR registration number: ACTRN12623000561684

This study is a multicentre, Type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation, superiority, parallel group, randomised controlled trial with a 1:1 randomisation to two arms: IV biosensor plus standard observation (intervention) or standard observation alone (control).

The primary objective of this study is to compare the effectiveness of a novel IV biosensor + standard observation vs standard observation alone in reducing extravasation injuries in hospitalised infants.

Participants who meet any of these criteria are not eligible for enrolment as trial participants: -Other types of vascular access devices, including midline catheters, peripheral arterial catheters and central venous catheters -Pre-existing skin condition affecting study peripheral IV site, e.g., i) atopic dermatitis or extensive erythema toxicum, ii) infectious diseases such as Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome; iii) burn (e.g., heat, decontamination); iv) inherited conditions such as epidermolysis bullosa, ichthyosis and aplasia cutis congenita -Previously enrolled in this study and randomised to one of the treatment conditions -Currently receiving end-of-life, redirection of care, and palliative care.

The primary outcome is any extravasation, measured using the 4-point Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Centre (CCHMC) Extravasation Harm Scale and then categorised as no harm vs any harm (that is, a composite of mild, moderate or severe harm) [1].

text.text: This scale combines physical (i.e., discolouration, swelling, redness, blisters, function, and arterial compromise), infusate properties (pH, osmolality, biological activity and volume) and injury treatment (scarring and surgical management) characteristics.
The primary outcome is the Outcome Assessment Committee's adjudicated rating; participants without a suspected injury referred to the Committee are classified as no harm.
These are the complications that occur during dwell, or at end of study completion, without failure, including: 1.
Infiltration/extravasation severity: using the 4-point CCHMC Extravasation Harm Scale (no harm vs mild vs moderate vs severe).
Infiltration/extravasation volume: measured by the surface area to limb length ratio and photographic imaging, including comparison to the non-affected limb.
Infiltration/extravasation injury pH and colour changes: measured by the MGC tool and non-invasive monitors (pH meter).

Infiltration/extravasation treatment: measured by count of the number and type of dressings, skin grafting and/or scar management, and duration of treatment including scar management (censored at 6 months).
Requirement for replacement PIVC: yes/no, at PIVC removal.
Time to PIVC failure: hours from insertion to removal for PIVC dysfunction.
PIVC dwell time: hours from insertion to removal for any reason.
Near infrared/heat-related skin injuries: at the PIVC site (IV biosensor group only).
Mechanical adhesive-related and/or pressure injuries: surrounding the PIVC site.
Overall quality of life: PedsQL™ Infant Scales or IQI total score at recruitment and PIVC removal.
Serious adverse events (safety outcome): in-trial mortality, severe extravasation or device-related injury.

An exploratory analysis, not prespecified in the protocol, will compare outcomes 1 and 2 between participants with and without a red alarm in the IV biosensor group with an extravasation injury (Section 3.4.11).

Data collection Data will be directly input by the Research Nurse into a purpose-built case report form (CRF) in REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture, Vanderbilt), hosted by the University of Queensland on password-protected devices.
The Research Nurses will follow participants daily until PIVC removal.
Data will be kept password-protected.

text.text: • At enrolment, Research Nurses will collect consent forms and data on patient characteristics (age, primary diagnosis, weight, skin colour, first or subsequent PIVC), provider characteristics (inserter workforce, insertion approach, planned device utility), PIVC characteristics (placement, location, catheter type, securement), and quality of life (PedsQL™ Infant Scales or IQI).
• Daily, Research Nurses will visit participants to assess for primary and secondary outcomes, current PIVC use, and any clinical, device or treatment factors changed since recruitment.

• Within 24 hours of PIVC removal, Research Nurses will collect data on PIVC dwell, reason for removal, PIVC dysfunction, need for replacement PIVC, near infrared skin injury, monitor alarms, mechanical adhesive related skin injury or pressure injury, serious adverse events including mortality, and quality of life.
If an infiltration/extravasation injury is identified, the PIVC site will be assessed and documented.
• If an infiltration/extravasation injury occurs, the patient will be followed every 24 hours, collecting data on injury characteristics, volume, treatment and sequelae, until the injury stabilises.

• For participants with a confirmed extravasation injury only, additional follow-up questionnaires (quality of life and modified Brisbane Burns Scar Impact Profile) will be collected at 1, 3, and 6 months post-PIVC removal.

text.text: All between-group regression models will include randomisation stratum (four levels) as a covariate, reflecting stratified randomisation.
If a stratum has too few events for a model to converge, the two SCUH strata will be combined.
Odds ratios and hazard ratios are therefore conditional on stratum.
Analyses will follow intention to treat, with the PIVC as the unit of analysis (one PIVC per child).
All randomised participants will be analysed in the group to which they were randomised, using all available data.
The primary outcome will be analysed as complete case.
As the primary outcome is assessed daily throughout dwell, missing primary outcome data are expected to be minimal, limited to participants who withdraw consent before any outcome assessment.
Participants transferred before PIVC removal will be included, with the outcome assessed up to transfer (Figure 4).

text.text: Safety outcomes will be reported for all randomised participants.
Per protocol analysis will be performed to test the sensitivity of the results to noncompliance.
This analysis will include participants who received their allocated intervention, excluding those with a protocol violation (Section 2.7).
The number of missing observations for each primary and secondary outcome will be reported by study group.
If the proportion of missing observations is non-trivial (>5%), consideration will be given to the possible introduction of compliance and attrition bias.
text.formatted: If the proportion of missing observations is non-trivial (>5%), consideration will be given to the possible introduction of compliance and attrition bias.

text.text: The cause of any missing data will be assessed.
For the primary outcome, between-group comparisons will be stratified by site to investigate the level of variability across sites.

We will test the heterogeneity between sites by running a model with treatment group and site as main effects, and a group-by-site interaction term, and will report the level of interaction using the likelihood ratio test.
Continuous data will be summarised descriptively using either mean and standard deviation (SD) or median and interquartile range (IQR), depending on the distribution of the variable of interest.
Categorical data will be presented as frequencies and percentages.
A two-sided significance level of 0.05 will be used for the primary outcome.
Secondary outcomes are exploratory; they will be reported with 95% CIs without adjustment for multiplicity.

For any outcome with >5% missing data, a sensitivity analysis will use multiple imputation by chained equations (20 imputed datasets), performed separately by randomised group, assuming data are missing at random, with imputation models including treatment group, randomisation stratum, the outcome, age, weight and prematurity.

text.text: Demographic and baseline characteristics will be reported descriptively by allocated study group.
Variable definitions are provided in Appendix 2 (data dictionary).

The primary outcome of any extravasation injury (no harm vs any harm on the CCHMC Extravasation Harm Scale) will be compared between groups using logistic regression, with treatment group (IV biosensor/standard care) as the main effect and randomisation stratum as a covariate.

The effect estimate will be the absolute risk difference with 95% confidence interval and P-value, estimated by standardisation over the stratum distribution of all randomised participants (Stata margins) [12].
text.formatted: The effect estimate will be the absolute risk difference with 95% confidence interval and P-value, estimated by standardisation over the stratum distribution of all randomised participants (Stata margins) <ref type="bibr">[12]</ref>.

text.text: The odds ratio (95% CI), conditional on stratum, will also be reported from the same model.
Infiltration/extravasation severity will be assessed using the 4-point CCHMC Extravasation Harm Scale, with each category (no harm, mild, moderate, or severe) compared.
The distribution of severity categories will be reported by group as frequencies and percentages.

An ordered logistic regression model with treatment group as the main effect and randomisation stratum as a covariate will be used to compare severity across groups, with results presented as odds ratios (95% CI).

Infiltration/extravasation volume, measured by the surface area to limb length ratio and photographic imaging (including comparison to the non-affected limb), will be summarised descriptively (median and IQR) by group for participants with an injury.
Measured by count of the number and type of dressings, skin grafting and/or scar management, and duration of treatment, including scar management (censored at 6 months).
As treatment is measured only in participants with an injury, the number and percentage of treatments will be reported descriptively by group, without between-group comparison.
Treatment data are recorded on the stabilisation and follow-up forms.
Measured by non-invasive monitors (pH Meter) and metric graduated colour (MGC) tool.
As these are measured only in participants with an injury, they will be summarised descriptively by group (pH: median and IQR; colour: number and percentage).

Requirement for replacement PIVC (yes, including unsuccessful attempts, vs no) will be reported as number and percentage per group for all participants and will be analysed using logistic regression with study group as the main effect.
The results will be presented as an odds ratio (95% CI).

Time to PIVC failure (removal for any PIVC dysfunction, including infiltration/extravasation) will be compared using Cox proportional hazards regression, with PIVCs removed at completion of therapy or for other reasons censored at removal.
Time will be measured from PIVC insertion, with participants entering the risk set at randomisation (delayed entry), as most PIVCs were inserted before enrolment.

Failure is recorded at the date and time of PIVC removal for dysfunction (infiltration/extravasation, other dysfunction, or a biosensor red alert); red alerts that did not lead to removal are not counted as failure.
Results will be presented as hazard ratios (95% CI) and Kaplan-Meier curves.
Dwell time (hours) will be summarised as median (IQR) by group and compared using quantile regression (median difference, 95% CI).

The number and percentage of devices that experience near infrared/heat-related skin injuries at the PIVC site will be reported descriptively (number and percentage) in the IV biosensor group only, as this injury can occur only with the sensor in place.

The number and percentage of devices experiencing mechanical adhesive-related skin injuries and pressure injuries surrounding the PIVC site will be calculated per group and analysed using logistic regression with study group as the main effect.
The results will be presented as an odds ratio (95% CI).

Measured at recruitment and PIVC removal by parent report, using the PedsQL™ Infant Scales (1-12 month version, 36 items) and/or the Infant Health-Related Quality of Life Instrument (IQI, 7 items); the IQI replaced the PedsQL™ from 23/05/2024.

The PedsQL™ total score will be calculated per the scoring manual (items reverse-scored and transformed to 0-100, higher scores indicating better quality of life), excluding items for infants over 13 months.
The IQI total score will be the sum of the seven item scores (range 7-28, higher scores indicating poorer health).
Total scores will be summarised by group (mean (SD) or median (IQR)) at both time points, separately for each instrument, among participants who completed it.
Between-group differences at PIVC removal will be estimated using linear regression adjusted for the baseline score and randomisation stratum, and presented as a mean difference (95% CI) for the IQI.
As few participants completed the PedsQL™, its scores will be reported descriptively.
Scores will be calculated when at least 50% of items are answered, per each instrument's scoring guidance.
Quality of life at 1, 3 and 6 months will be reported with the health economic evaluation.

The number and percentage of participants experiencing a serious adverse event will be reported per group and compared using Firth penalised logistic regression adjusted for randomisation stratum, presented as an odds ratio (95% CI), if at least one serious adverse event occurs; otherwise serious adverse events will be reported as counts.
All serious adverse events will be reported narratively.

Among participants in the IV biosensor group with an extravasation injury, extravasation severity (CCHMC) and volume will be compared between those with and without a red alarm before injury identification.
Results will be summarised descriptively (n, %; median, IQR); if numbers permit, ordinal logistic regression (severity) and linear or quantile regression (volume) will be used.
As this comparison is not randomised, it is hypothesis generating only.
Alarms will be classed as preceding injury when an alarm time precedes the recorded time of injury identification; only the first three alarm times per daily check are recorded.
